    #122730. Senate Dems dismiss talk of earlier leadership election; Schumer confident

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1425 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Senate Dems dismiss talk of earlier leadership election; Schumer confident

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1425 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov.
    • It has been revealed that senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a newly introduced majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec.
    • That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., leaves the Senate Democrats’ lunch meeting in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    It has been revealed that senate Democrats moved Tuesday to squelch talk of an accelerated timeline for the vote for a newly introduced majority leader, signaling they intend to keep the contest on Dec. 1.

    That the timing of the vote was already becoming a flashpoint in the caucus speaks to the rocky start for the incoming majority despite a near-sweep of key midterm races that could give Democrats 56 seats in the chamber.

    The prospect of an earlier vote had been floated as a way to prevent internal divisions from hobbling the incoming majority before the 120th Congress even began.

    Industry observers note that but supporters of Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., both in the chamber and among party activists outside it, were increasingly casting the idea of a shorter contest as a bid to halt momentum for his bid against Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y.

    Even as Schumer maintained that he has the votes necessary to be elected as majority leader, several senators insisted Tuesday the discussion taking place within the caucus was a good thing.

    “I’m confident I’ll be the next leader. I have the votes,” Schumer told reporters on Tuesday following the conference’s lunch.

    Van Hollen for his part told reporters Tuesday he believes his bid has “momentum at this point in time, which is why there was an effort to short-circuit the process.”.

    “And fortunately, I think that will fail.”.

    Several senators leaving the meeting remarked the topic of the leadership contest did not come up at all, and that neither Van Hollen nor Schumer gave a presentation regarding their bids.

    According to recent reports, that was in large part due to the absence of the incoming senators — which could be as high as 13, depending on how the dust settles in Alaska — who are able to vote in the leadership elections. Retiring senators do not cast a ballot.

    With such a large class of incoming freshman, several incumbents saw it crucial to keep the election scheduled as is.

    In a recent development, “No one has ever raised that with me. I mean, I saw a rumor that some were wanting to contemplate that,” Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., said Tuesday after the meeting. “The leadership discussions did not come up today. And part of the reason is we didn’t have the newcomers.”.

    “Remember, they all get a vote in the leadership discussion, and it would be hard to get them here,” Kaine continued, noting that only Sen.-elect Scott Colom, D-Miss., was present for Tuesday’s lunch amid his belated orientation. “But nobody else was here, and that discussion needs to have the newcomers because newcomers get votes. The outgoers don’t, right?”.

    In a recent development, sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M. echoed that sentiment on Monday evening, saying, “I want to hear from the freshman class as well.”.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said, “I don’t know that” when asked about moving up the elections. “I think that we need to make sure that there’s enough time for what I would call a robust discussion about what we’re going to do. I think we should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here, and I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard.

    “They’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table,” she stated.

    Several senators-elect are among those who have publicly thrown their hats into Van Hollen’s corner, including Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota and Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan.El-Sayed on Tuesday said at The Atlantic Summit that he sees Van Hollen as “unique” in his experience in the Senate and running the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee as well as what he called “a willingness to take risks.”.

    “We need people who are willing to take legislative risk,” he mentioned. “We need to rethink the way we legislate. It just should not be the process where you make one or two omnibus pieces of legislation that nobody really knows what’s in them,” he continued, advocating for piecemeal legislation.

    According to recent reports, but there are about 15 Democrats who have publicly backed Schumer’s bid. If former Rep. Mary Peltola maintains her lead in the lone outstanding Senate race in Alaska, Schumer would need 29 to secure the helm of the ship.

    Industry observers note that “I committed to Sen. Schumer literally months ago, and I continue to support him,” Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., stated Monday. “I’m incredibly excited about the new ideas that our new colleagues have, and their energy, and the potential for changing the way we operate in the Senate, which we have to do because we need to be more effective.”.

    Sources indicate that several incumbents have also thrown their support behind Van Hollen for leadership change, including Sens. Jeff Merkley of Oregon and Bernie Sanders of Vermont.“I think, as I’ve said many times, the American people want change in the way we do business here in Washington, and I think Chris Van Hollen would be a great leader of the Democrats,” Sanders said Monday.

    Several senators and senators-elect are refusing to comment publicly on who they’ll back.

    Industry observers note that that included Sen. Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., who noted he wants “to hear the commitments from folks that are pursuing this leadership role as well as every leadership position in the Senate, as well as chairs of committees, to what their commitments are to having a strong agenda that’s going to improve people’s lives.”.

    Kaine is also in that camp, and insisted Monday he hadn’t made up his mind. But he did speak positively of Schumer’s recruiting efforts in the midterms and history of dealing with a Trump White House.

    “Schumer just delivered a major win for us. No one who was not on the ballot worked harder for this victory than Chuck Schumer,” he remarked. “Chuck Schumer also happens to know Donald Trump better than anybody else in the caucus, and dealing with this wounded president is going to be a challenge over the next few years.”.

    Industry observers note that “The voters are also overwhelmingly demanding change,” he stated. “So we got to figure that out as a caucus, and we’re going to be able to. And we’re not afraid to have a discussion because we’re Democrats. We like democracy.”.

    Sources indicate that sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., also remained mum on who he’ll support but stated, “You can’t argue” Schumer brought Democrats the majority.

    “I think it’s a healthy thing to try and improve how the conference goes about its business,” he noted. “I don’t think that is a distraction. We can deal with some distractions. We have to keep our eye on the ball.”.

    Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., who last week called for new leadership in a news conference with Sanders, days before Van Hollen’s announcement, was noncommittal arriving to the Capitol on Monday if that meant she’d be supporting the Maryland Democrat.

    Senate Democrats’ election will most likely be a secret ballot. And most senators remained unified against moving the leadership elections before they recess for the Thanksgiving break.

    According to recent reports, “They should not be moved up. There was a reason that those rule changes took place before, and they should take place in December,” Lujan stated.

    Kaine dismissed Van Hollen’s challenge as anything unusual.

    It has been revealed that “We’re Democrats. It’s frankly unusual that there usually [aren’t] challenges to Democratic leaders because we’re Democrats,” he said. “It’s been a little unusual to have been here for 13 years and not really have them like this. But I think it’s a discussion not just about the two contenders for the leader role, but also the leadership team and priorities, and it’s all wrapped up in one discussion.”.

    “That’s why we decided, don’t do these votes until December, because you want to let the election settle and understand exactly what’s up, and then hear from potential votes.”.

    Sen. Andy Kim, D-N.J., said, “I think we should stick with the rules when it comes to the caucus. … That’s going to be what makes sure that we show that we have a real process.”.

    Sanders asked: “Why would anyone want to do that?” when asked.

    “I think there’s a date that’s been called, and that should be the date.”.

    Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that A fresh-hire Delta Air Lines pilot reportedly answered his cellphone while taxiing for departure, prompting the captain to return to the gate and have him removed. According to an account shared on the Black Box Aviation Podcast, the first officer subsequently lost his job. If accurate, this was a remarkably poor way to begin an airline career at Delta!

    The story comes from the Black Box Aviation Podcast, which recently discussed distractions on the flight deck and the consequences of using personal phones while working.

    According to the account, a Delta first officer was undergoing Initial Operating Experience, or IOE, when he answered his cellphone while the aircraft was taxiing for departure. Rather than continue to the runway, the captain returned to the gate. The first officer was removed and reportedly fired.

    IOE involves flying actual airline trips under the supervision of a check pilot. A new hire may have substantial flying experience elsewhere, but is still learning how to apply the new airline’s procedures in everyday operations.

    It has been revealed that new-hire FO. First trip on the line. Taxiing out in Atlanta… and his phone rings. 📵Silence it? Nope. He ANSWERED it. 🤦‍♂️Captain went back to the gate, and that was the end of his dream job.🎧 Watch the full episode in the comments 👇#PilotLife #AirlinePilot #AvGeek pic.twitter.com/QefwSoTBiN.

    — The Blackbox Podcast (@the_black_box01) November 17, 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that there are limitations to this account. I have not obtained confirmation from Delta (understandably, no response). Furthermore, no flight number or date was referenced, so the recent discussion does not necessarily imply that this just happened. The reported dismissal should be understood as the podcast’s account…and incidents like this have been part of airline pilot lore in online forums for many years.

    I suspect some passengers might hear this story and think firing someone over a phone call sounds excessive. After all, the airplane was still on the ground.

    But taxiing requires the attention of both pilots. A captain may be steering, but the first officer still has work to do, including monitoring the aircraft’s progress and air traffic control instructions. A wrong turn or missed runway instruction can have very serious consequences…being a pilot is one of the professions that leaves no room for error.

    It has been revealed that the federal sterile cockpit rule specifically includes taxi among the critical phases of flight. It prohibits activities that could distract flight crew members from their duties.

    A separate provision restricts the use of personal wireless communications devices at a flight crew duty station during flight, with exceptions for specified purposes under approved airline procedures. The FAA’s guidance makes clear that prohibited personal use includes telephone conversations, texting, and browsing the internet.

    According to recent reports, pilots can use approved electronic flight bags (EFBs are the iPads that replace paper manuals and charts) and make necessary operational communications. Taking an ordinary personal call while taxiing is another matter.

    I spend far too much time on my phone, as my weekly screen time reports reminds me every Sunday morning. I understand how reflexively we reach for it when it rings or lights up. But there are times when it simply needs to remain put away, and working in the cockpit of a moving passenger jet is certainly one of them.

    Recent findings suggest that what strikes me about this account is the setting. This was reportedly a fresh hire being supervised during training. That should be a time to demonstrate that you understand the procedures and can be trusted to follow them!

    In a recent development, if the account is complete and the call was personal, I understand why the captain would have concerns about continuing the flight with that first officer. Returning to the gate would inconvenience passengers, but I would rather be delayed than have a captain continue after losing confidence in the person beside him.

    It has been revealed that the employment decision is harder to assess without the full record. We do not know whether there were previous concerns or what explanation the first officer offered. I tend to be more forgiving and don’t think that every mistake during training should end a career. Even so, this would be a serious lapse in judgment. A pilot arriving at Delta should already understand why answering a personal call during taxi is unacceptable.

    In a recent development, the Black Box Aviation Podcast recounts a Delta newly introduced-hire first officer answering his cellphone during taxi, being removed after a return to the gate, and subsequently losing his job. The incident remains unconfirmed beyond that account.

    In a recent development, if it happened as described, I understand the captain’s decision. Passengers should be able to expect both pilots to give their attention to operating the aircraft safely. Answering personal phone call is unacceptable.

    Tech Report: We Tracked 133 Diverted Flights In Two Weeks: Here’s Where They Ended Up

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Flight diversions are often treated as isolated incidents, but a closer look at two weeks of aviation activity reveals a much larger pattern.
    • According to recent reports, simple Flying Flight Tracker data examined 63 diversion posts covering 133 flights, including 17 major diversion waves involving four or more aircraft from the same airport within an hour.
    • In a recent development, thursday, November 12, was easily the busiest day in our tracking period, accounting for 35 of the 63 diversion posts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Flight diversions are often treated as isolated incidents, but a closer look at two weeks of aviation activity reveals a much larger pattern. Between November 6 and 18, 133 flights diverted from their intended destinations, and several airports saw multiple waves of diversions within hours. Some aircraft landed relatively close to their original destinations, while others ended up thousands of kilometers away.

    According to recent reports, simple Flying Flight Tracker data examined 63 diversion posts covering 133 flights, including 17 major diversion waves involving four or more aircraft from the same airport within an hour. From an 11-flight disruption at Newly introduced York-JFK to a 13-aircraft scramble at San Francisco International Airport (SFO), the data reveals which airports absorbed the most diverted traffic, where airlines sent their aircraft, and which journeys experienced the most dramatic changes.

    In a recent development, thursday, November 12, was easily the busiest day in our tracking period, accounting for 35 of the 63 diversion posts. The disruptions were particularly concentrated around Latest York, where John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) saw an 11-flight diversion wave, along with numerous additional diversions involving transatlantic arrivals.

    Recent findings suggest that the disruption was noticeable among international operators. Aircraft arriving from Europe were redirected to airports across the northeastern United States, with Boston Logan International Airport (BOS) becoming the most frequently used alternative. Other aircraft were diverted to Bradley International Airport (BDL) in Connecticut, Philadelphia International Airport (PHL), Providence, and, of course, Bangor International Airport (BGR) in Maine, which has historically been a major diversion hotspot for many transatlantic flights. The diversions affected flights operated by several major airlines, including American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, British Airways, Air France, Lufthansa, and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines.

    Industry observers note that the JFK disruption was not the only significant event that day. The neighboring Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) experienced a four-flight diversion wave, while PHL saw eight flights redirected. LaGuardia Airport (LGA) also recorded four diversions. Together, these events demonstrate how disruption at several airports in the same metropolitan region can create a complicated situation for airline operations. But with so many aircraft needing alternative landing locations, which airports handled the most diversions?

    It has been revealed that boston was the most frequently used diversion airport during the tracking period, receiving 16 flights that had originally been scheduled to land elsewhere. Much of this traffic came from the November 12 disruption at JFK, when transatlantic arrivals were redirected to alternative airports across the northeastern United States.

    Boston's geographical position made it a prominent destination in the diversion data. Several flights originally scheduled to land at JFK were redirected there, including services operated by American, Delta, British Airways, Air France, Emirates, and KLM. The affected routes included arrivals from London, Amsterdam, Paris Charles de Gaulle, Barcelona, Milan, and Dubai. However, Boston was not the only airport dealing with repeated waves of unexpected arrivals.

    On the other side of the Atlantic, Katowice International Airport (KTW) in Poland came remarkably close to the top, receiving 15 diverted flights. The airport became an notable alternative for aircraft originally scheduled to land at Krakow John Paul II International Airport (KRK), which experienced four separate diversion waves over four consecutive days. Back in the US, Fresno Yosemite International Airport (FAT) ranked third, receiving nine diverted aircraft, all tied to the major San Francisco disruption on November 18.

    Boston Logan International Airport.

    Fresno Yosemite International Airport.

    Washington Dulles International Airport.

    Los Angeles International Airport.

    The geographical distribution is rather curious. Boston and Katowice were heavily affected by disruptions at nearby airports, while Fresno and Los Angeles benefited from their proximity to San Francisco. This raises another question: were these diversions isolated incidents, or were entire airports experiencing repeated operational disruptions?

    In a recent development, krakow was one of the most interesting airports in the dataset, experiencing four separate diversion waves between November 6 and 9. Each wave involved at least four flights, with the aircraft redirected to several alternative airports across Poland and neighboring countries.

    The first wave occurred late on November 6, when four aircraft originally scheduled to land at Krakow were redirected. Three ended up at Katowice, while the fourth landed at Rzeszow-Jasionka Airport (RZE). The following morning, another six flights were diverted, with five heading to Katowice and one returning to Frankfurt. This included aircraft operated by Ryanair, Wizz Air, and Finnair, demonstrating that the disruption affected multiple airlines and aircraft types.

    Recent findings suggest that the situation continued on November 8, when two further waves involved eight and five aircraft, respectively. Unlike the earlier events, these diversions were distributed across a wider selection of cities, including Warsaw, Wroclaw, Gdansk, Brno, and Ostrava. The final wave arrived on November 9, when another six flights were redirected, five of which landed at Katowice.

    Katowice, Warsaw, Wroclaw, Gdansk, Rzeszow, Ostrava.

    Wroclaw, Warsaw-Modlin, Brno, Lodz, Ostrava.

    Katowice's 15-flight total is particularly revealing because it highlights how an airport can become an important alternative landing point during repeated disruption at a nearby facility. However, Krakow was not the only airport to experience a concentrated wave of diversions. On November 18, events unfolded on the opposite side of the Atlantic, producing the largest individual diversion wave recorded in our dataset.

    In a recent development, on November 18, SFO saw the largest individual diversion wave in our tracking period, with 13 flights redirected in about an hour. Nine aircraft landed at Fresno, while another four were sent to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

    The scale of the event was striking because it involved both domestic and international services. Among the affected aircraft was Korean Air flight 23 from Seoul Incheon (ICN), which landed in LAX instead SFO. Other long-haul services included United Airlines flight 862 from Hong Kong, which also diverted to LAX, and United flight UA34 from Osaka Kansai, which followed the same route.

    In a recent development, domestic arrivals were affected too. JetBlue flight 633 from BOS and AA76 from JFK both landed at Fresno. DL668, arriving from JFK, was among the aircraft redirected to LAX. The nine-flight Fresno total made it the most frequently used alternative airport during the San Francisco event.

    The November 18 San Francisco diversion wave:.

    Fresno Yosemite International Airport (FAT).

    Los Angeles International Airport (LAX).

    Fresno's role and location are noteworthy. Although it is considerably smaller than San Francisco and Los Angeles, it absorbed most of the diverted aircraft in this event. This highlights how diversion planning can extend beyond a region's largest airports, depending on operational circumstances and available alternatives. However, the San Francisco wave was not the only event involving unusually long journeys to alternative airports. Some aircraft in our dataset ended up nowhere near their original destinations.

    According to recent reports, although many diversions involved relatively short journeys to nearby airports, several flights in our dataset experienced substantially longer route changes. The most dramatic example involved KL677, which was operating from AMS to Calgary International Airport (YYC).

    Recent findings suggest that on November 9, the Boeing 787 operating the service landed at Keflavik International Airport (KEF), in Iceland, approximately 3,200 miles (5,132 kilometers) short of its intended destination. This was the longest diversion recorded in our dataset. The distance illustrates just how significant the operational consequences of a diversion can become when an aircraft is already deep into a long-haul journey.

    In a recent development, united Airlines flight UA114 experienced the second-longest diversion. The service was scheduled to fly from Papeete International Airport (PPT), in French Polynesia, to San Francisco, but instead landed at Honolulu International Airport (HNL). The aircraft arrived about (2,400 miles) 3,857 kilometers short of San Francisco, leaving passengers in Hawaii instead of the intended Californian destination.

    Recent findings suggest that the third-largest diversion involved easyJet flight 7883, operating from AMS to Tenerife South Airport (TFS). Instead of reaching the Canary Islands, the aircraft landed at Paris Orly Airport (ORY), approximately 1,750 miles (2,814 kilometers) from its intended destination, much closer to the departure airport. The flight was unusual because it involved a European short-haul operator and a diversion just within 300 miles (about 500 km) of the departure point.

    The three longest diversions recorded:.

    These examples demonstrate that a diversion does not necessarily mean landing at the nearest available airport. Long-haul operations can involve complex considerations, and aircraft operating across different regions may have to use alternative airports far from their original destinations. But how representative are these individual examples of the overall diversion picture?

    The 133 flights recorded between November 6 and 18 provide an interesting snapshot of how quickly disruption can spread across airline networks. Simple Flying's tracking identified 63 separate diversion posts, including 17 major waves in which at least four aircraft were diverted from the same airport within an hour. The dataset also contained 45 long-haul diversion posts and one short-haul diversion involving easyJet.

    It has been revealed that it is key to distinguish between the number of posts and the number of flights. A single diversion-wave post could cover several aircraft, while individual long-haul diversions were also reported separately. Some long-haul flights were included in the larger waves, meaning the figures should not be added together as independent flight totals. ADS-B tracking independently confirmed the landing airports for every flight included in the spreadsheet.

    It has been revealed that simple Flying Flight Tracker's social channels regularly publish individual diversions and larger waves of disrupted flights as they happen. They offer a useful way to follow unexpected changes to airline operations in real time.

    The most interesting finding isn't that 133 aircraft landed somewhere other than their planned destinations. It is how concentrated some of the disruption became. Boston absorbed 16 diverted flights, Katowice received 15, and Fresno handled nine aircraft during a single event at San Francisco. With individual waves involving as many as 13 aircraft, the data reminds us that an airport's operational importance can change dramatically when another facility is disrupted.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is set 24 years before the action of the first film and tells the origin story of Katniss Everdeen’s grumpy tutor, Haymitch Abernathy, as he enters the Games himself.

    Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy and Whitney Peak as Lenore Dove Baird.

    Based on the books by Suzanne Collins, the dystopian series is set in a futuristic America in which each district must send a teenage tribute to fight to the death in an annual competition—the idea being that, by doing so, the public will be too afraid to rebel against President Snow.

    This edition of the games is known as the Quarter Quell, with double the number of tributes being sent into the arena, meaning the stakes are so much higher. Interest in the film is high, not least because Haymitch is so beloved in the original series, portrayed by Woody Harrelson. Newcomer Joseph Zada takes the lead role in the latest film, while Hollywood heavyweights Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, Elle Fanning, and Kieran Culkin also star.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the most key sets in the film is the arena where the games take place, and for this, director Francis Lawrence opted not for CGI and a green screen, but instead a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in northern Spain. Below, we look into the locations used in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Ben Wang as Wyatt Callow, Percy Daggs IV as Ampert Latier, Joseph Zada as Haymitch Abernathy, and Mckenna Grace as Maysilee Donner in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Within the book and film series, the settings for the Hunger Games are always known to be virtually spectacular. For this film, filmmakers settled on the vast and untouched landscape of Somiedo Natural Park in the Asturias region of northern Spain, which boasts mountain ranges, glacial valleys, beautiful meadows, dense forests, and tranquil lakes. The remote region is also home to the last brown bear population in Europe.

    When the tributes are rolled out into the arena, they are presented with a vast Cornucopia, a pile of weapons, food, and other supplies that might be useful to them in the competition. These scenes were filmed at Somiedo Natural Park, with the Asturian mountains and a glacial lake in the background.

    “Somiedo is a spectacular place,” said Pedro Aráez, supervising location manager. “The valleys, forests, and mountains have a very wild, untouched feeling, which was exactly what the filmmakers were looking for. It’s remote, dramatic, and visually unique. When you arrive there, you immediately understand why it was chosen.”.

    Recent findings suggest that located close to Somiedo, the Teverga beech forest, Hayedo de Montegrande, was used for some of the dense woodland scenes, in which contestants battle it out and hide in the woods. Other scenes filmed here utilized a series of glacial lakes, the Saliencia Lakes and the Lago de la Cueva.

    Iris Apatow as Proserpina Trinket and Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

    Before the tributes are released into the arena, they are first held in special little pods underground which are arranged in a circle around the Cornucopia. The perfect location for this? A velodrome, of course, which is steeply circular so cyclists can race around it. The film crew utilized Berlin’s Velodrom for this very purpose, with its cold, clinical silver decor perfect for matching the hi-tech aesthetic associated with the Capitol.

    Ralph Fiennes as President Snow.

    Prior to entering the Games, tributes must introduce themselves on the public stage, during a televised grand chariot parade in the Capitol. Another Berlin location with links to the sporting world was used for this purpose: the Olympiastadion. For fans of the earlier films, this is the moment when Jennifer Lawrence’s character Katniss becomes “the girl on fire” with her incredible flaming dress.

    Sources indicate that the futuristic architecture of Edificio Calatrava in Oviedo, Spain—with its striking, claw-like structure—stands in for a building in the Capitol, where President Snow and his government live. The complex was designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, whose work is known for resembling living organisms. Meanwhile, the 14th-century Ehreshoven Castle, just outside of Cologne, was also used as a filming location, with local press reporting that its lush interiors might have been used to stand in for somewhere inside the Capitol.

    A former smelting factory complex in western Germany, Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord provides the backdrop for one of the most atmospheric settings in the films, Haymitch’s home of District 12. The vast complex is able to stand in for multiple places within the district, a former mining town that has fallen on seriously bad times. Rather than being a desolate area stumbled upon by the filmmakers, Landschaftspark is popular for its nightly light installation by British artist Jonathan Park. There are also regular al fresco events here, from film screenings to the annual art-meets-sport Ruhr Games and Traumzeit Festival. Another location in Germany, Lindlar Quarry, was used for District 12, with wooden huts built here to resemble the outskirts of the village.

    A version of this story originally appeared in Condé Nast Traveller UK.

    #122723. Which AI Bots Can Help You Book Travel?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1957 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Which AI Bots Can Help You Book Travel?

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A multitude of newly introduced start ups promise AI assistants will “handle your travel.” I’m skeptical of anything that promises to handle my travel, mostly because I’ve spent years learning exactly where airline websites like to hide the landmines and sharing it with our audience.
    • To be clear, this is not a test of chatbots that spit out a list of flights and then send you off to do the work yourself.
    • I gave the a Grok Bot (a single AI agent) the same basic trip on every airline: Pittsburgh (PIT) to Fort Myers (RSW), one way, on Tuesday, December 15, 2026, for four adults.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A multitude of newly introduced start ups promise AI assistants will “handle your travel.” I’m skeptical of anything that promises to handle my travel, mostly because I’ve spent years learning exactly where airline websites like to hide the landmines and sharing it with our audience. But following Kirby’s (United’s) statement that AI bots would be blocked from its sites, I got curious about where we are with airlines and bots. I wanted to see what happens when an AI agent, one that drives a real web browser the way you or I would (in this case, Grok as ChatGPT, and Claude work differently), sits down at the airline’s own website and tries to book a real itinerary.

    To be clear, this is not a test of chatbots that spit out a list of flights and then send you off to do the work yourself. The question here is narrower and more practical. Can an agentic AI search, pick a fare, fill in the forms and get a family of four to the payment page without a human bailing it out? And just as interesting, which airlines let it in the door at all? For this hypothesis, I presumed United would be a certain “no” but what about the others?

    I gave the a Grok Bot (a single AI agent) the same basic trip on every airline: Pittsburgh (PIT) to Fort Myers (RSW), one way, on Tuesday, December 15, 2026, for four adults. On American, I used a real award rebooking for my own family while signed in to my AAdvantage account. On Delta, United and Southwest, the agent shopped cash fares while signed out. Grok is unique in two ways, first that it has its “own computer” where it runs your searches instead of yours, and second, that it can securely store your login credentials and operate as you would but it never sees those credentials (don’t ask me how.) I understand that Muse may have some of the same features, but my setup experience there was not as straight forward and I don’t need a fifth AI tool even if it’s integrated into my existing Instagram and Facebook accounts.

    I drew one firm line. The agent could go as far as the passenger or payment page, but nothing got purchased in any of these tests. Card details, CVVs and the final “Purchase” click stayed with me and I never processed any of them.

    American was the most realistic test and also the most frustrating. The agent had no trouble with the award search on aa.com using my account logged in. It pulled up 40 results for PIT to RSW, with Main Cabin at 10,500 miles one way per person and First at 25,500 miles.

    Sources indicate that it found AA 3030 acceptable flights from Pittsburgh to Charlotte, connecting to Fort Myers, in Main Cabin for 42,000 miles plus $22.40 for all four of us. If I wanted to, I could train the AI to understand whether I would want a morning or evening flight typically, an acceptable layover range, it could look at my schedule and ensure that we have sufficient time to get to a meeting and work around my schedule and preferences, not just my price. This test didn’t need all of that.

    Recent findings suggest that it got that itinerary all the way to “Review and pay.” Then the friction started. My saved card on the account required the CVV to be entered again, which the agent could not supply (and, frankly, should not have). While that was being sorted out, the checkout session expired.

    When the agent rebuilt the cart, aa.com threw up its “Please confirm you’re a human” challenge with an “I’m not a robot” box. The AI dutifully lied but identified where and how that was running. That page comes from a bot manager, which assigns every visitor a score from human to bot and can raise that score as the same visitor keeps making requests. Rebuilding a cart several times looks automated (because it was.) At that point a human had to step in.

    I’d rate this as a 90% solution with a final human check and ultimate purchase as the last 10% to complete. This is likely a best case scenario to keep control of your miles or money and ensure what you book is correct.

    Delta was the cleanest run of the bunch. The agent set up the one-way search, added four passengers, picked the date and landed on a results page with flights connecting in Atlanta and arriving after 9pm, at $192 per person in Main because this one was not a logged in redemption.

    From there it handled the Basic vs Main Classic choice, clicked past the upsell screens (an airline’s worst nightmare) and reached “Review and Pay” with a trip total of just under $965 for four in Main Classic. No captcha, no “are you human”, nothing. If Delta’s site was suspicious of my agent, it did not show it. There was no resistance. I flag this as an advantage for Delta, because tech forward clients will love that they can get an entire booking done start to finish without their intervention.

    United, like Delta, also let the agent through to the end of my test, but it took more attempts. The date field was finicky, with the calendar jumping ahead to January and February 2027 before the agent got back to December as I watched it work. The travelers dialog took several retries before it stopped saying “1 Adult” and accepted four. Not as smooth as Delta, but not a total block which I would have thought they’d install.

    Industry observers note that once the search ran, the agent took the first result (which it did not do for the others) a 6 AM departure via Washington Dulles, and correctly skipped Basic Economy (United makes you tick a “Basic Economy works for me” box first) in favor of the Standard fare. That is a reasonable choice for a family, but my kids would have something to say about a 6 AM departure, which is a good reminder that an AI agent only knows the preferences you give it.

    It then reached the “Traveler Info” page with a total of $964.80, which is, amusingly (but from a competitive standpoint, unsurprising), the exact same total Delta demonstrated for four people. No captcha appeared on United at any point.

    Southwest ended up with the best itinerary and the lowest price. The first result was a nonstop leaving Pittsburgh at 9:50 AM and arriving in Fort Myers at 12:30 PM. The agent chose the Choice fare at $222 per person, for a total of $885.60 for four. If it only it knew my kids, this nonstop would be the clear winner even if the price wasn’t better than United and Delta. That mentioned, I would also need to input information about what’s preferred when comparing miles and points, and my personal valuation so that it doesn’t choose even an $885 one-way for four people if American happened to be running 5,000-mile one-ways.

    Still, it got to the “Passengers” page, step 2 of 5, without any bot restrictions.

    Industry observers note that this isn’t an entirely comprehensively list as not all of them were useful for both the Live And Let’s Fly audience as well as my purposes. But what I did do is ask the AI to check whether each airline has its own AI assistants that can actually search, book, change or cancel a flight, or whether those tools just answer FAQs and hand you to a person.

    Alaska is the one that has built something close to a trip-planning AI. Its “Trip inspiration with AI” tool, Alaska Inspires, sits in the Book menu on alaskaair.com. Alaska and Microsoft (I suspect an even further neutered version of Co-Pilot) say you can type or speak a request in plain language, get destination ideas, and discover, compare and book in the same flow. In a March 2025 interview, Alaska’s director of innovation, Bernadette Berger, gave examples like “Where can I go in Europe for under 80k miles?” Microsoft’s write-up claims a 7% conversion rate versus 5% for the standard booking widget. My AI was not able to run my booking through Inspires so this would be a failure in my experience but I am willing to try again using different parameters.

    JetBlue does have a customer-service AI but I was unsuccessful in attempting to advance it further.

    Breeze Airways has gone further on digital customer care than most low-cost carriers. VP of Guest Experience Danny Cox, notes Breeze uses Gladly’s generative “Answer Threads” tool to present change and cancellation options in chat or SMS, and that AI fully resolves 37% of conversations. That is post-booking help, not a bot that will shop a latest itinerary for you. Breeze’s own contact pages blocked my lookup, so I could not independently confirm how the current chat or text flow works for a brand-new booking. That would be a failure but again, I suspect a logged in account might perform better.

    Allegiant does put a bot on its site but this is for customer service alone. Sun Country and JSX are even thinner on the consumer-facing side and my bot failed for all of these carriers too.

    On the cash side, AI agents can already do the boring part of booking. All three cash bookings reached a passenger or payment page, and none of them hit a captcha. The agent picked sensible fares, navigated upsell screens and dealt with clunky widgets on its own, even if United’s date picker and Southwest’s sluggish buttons cost it some time. Adding that personal context could make this a very practical option.

    The real wall is at the end. Payment details, CVVs and timed checkout sessions are designed to need a human, and I think that is fine. The bigger issue is bot detection because it wasn’t really built to detect or negate AI bots but general hacks that could operate massive attacks on the sites. American is the airline that blocked my agent outright, and it happened on the most complex booking of the test, involving award miles and a signed-in account. Whether that was because of the account, the repeated cart rebuilds or just AA’s settings that day, the result was the same.

    But United is the only one that has noted it won’t allow AI bots and absolutely did.

    It has been revealed that out of all of the tests, Delta was the easiest and had me most encouraged, while United and Southwest made it harder but not impossible and not specifically against AI, just the design of the site. American was the only one that really made it difficult and that shocked me. This test, and travelers using these tools for booking purposes are narrow at the moment but as AI agents/bots continue to advance and become normalized, the carriers will likely do something more robust. That stated, there could be a strong advantage for those that are “AI-friendly.” Competitive markets like Los Angeles and Fresh York might see more flights sold on Delta from indifferent travelers solely because it’s easier. The real question becomes how comfortable the general public becomes and with that, hopefully not too comfortable or websites will crash from consumers searching flights hundreds of times a day.

    Sources indicate that what do you think? Would you store your logins? Would you entrust an AI bot or agent to return travel results for you even if you have to complete the purchase on your own?

    #122722. Industry News: The Best Hotels Near Disneyland Paris With Cinderella Suites, 'Toy Story'–Themed Rooms, and Quaint Cottages

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1750 w)

    Industry News: The Best Hotels Near Disneyland Paris With Cinderella Suites, 'Toy Story'–Themed Rooms, and Quaint Cottages

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home.
    • There's also never been a better time to visit.
    • Of course, you'll need somewhere to rest your head at night, and that's where the best hotels near Disneyland Paris come into play.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home. Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, pair timeless charm with an ease you'll never find stateside. Here, you can sip Champagne in front of Sleeping Beauty's castle—or visit a dragon beneath it—while filling your days with delightful architecture, unprecedented thrills, and the wildest wilderness ride Disney's ever built (Substantial Thunder Mountain!).

    There's also never been a better time to visit. Walt Disney Studios Park's March 2026 transformation into the new Disney Adventure World brought a drone-filled nighttime show, Avengers coaster, and even a Frozen-themed land featuring a lifelike Olaf robot to its once-faltering second gate. Now, between Fantasyland classics and futuristic favorites, there's something new and thrilling for the entire family to experience.

    Of course, you'll need somewhere to rest your head at night, and that's where the best hotels near Disneyland Paris come into play. Staying at a Disney-branded property typically affords guests special amenities including ticket packages, exclusive character meet-and-greets, and Extra Magic Time, which provides bonus time in the parks prior to opening. These hotels are great options, but can also be pricey—luckily, there are also a few non-branded properties in the area that make for great alternatives. There's something here for everyone and every budget.

    Unsure of whether you want to add something so Américain to your Paris vacation? As a theme park journalist who has visited all Disney parks worldwide, trust me: It's worth the visit. Even with so many cultural monuments in Paris, nothing is more delightfully uncanny than witnessing the United States section of It's a Small World. So, whether you're looking for glamour or simply a good location, read on for the very best hotels near Disneyland Paris.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Three-minute walk.

    Industry observers note that as the crown jewel of France's Disney resort, this 487-room property is Disney's best hotel overseas—and, quite possibly, in the entire world. After undergoing an extensive three-year overhaul, the iconic pink palace reopened in 2024 with princess suites and luxurious amenities worthy of its five-star ranking. Great for couples or families, guests can anticipate the ultimate royal treatment thanks to rooms with romantic castle views just steps from the park. With kids treatments at the Spa by Clarins and two complimentary hours of childcare each day, parents can unwind at the Fleur de Lys bar, enjoy a prix fixe meal at chef Jean Imbert's on-site restaurant, or perhaps even sneak back into the parks themselves. (We won't tell.).

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Eight-minute drive.

    Recent findings suggest that rustic-chic in the best of ways, Marriott's Village d'Île-de-France offers cozy abodes that sleep up to eight with full kitchens, washing machines, and plenty of space to stretch out, all a short shuttle ride from the theme parks. Designed to emulate the charms of a small Parisian village, these quaint studios and multi-bedroom town houses feel more like cottages than traditional vacation rentals. Surroundings like these may sound quotidien to someone like Princess Belle, but the resort is as sweet as the rooms are spacious, making it an ideal choice for a hotel near Disneyland Paris as well as extended trips to nearby towns.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    Recent findings suggest that considering it's the only hotel in the world dedicated to Marvel's famed comic book characters, it's no surprise the Infinity Stone–colored beverages and slick, silver rooms at Disney Hotel New York - The Art of Marvel are somewhat out of this world. Family-friendly amenities like superhero meet-and-greets and a design studio with character drawing experiences make it the ultimate getaway for any comic book–obsessed fan in your family. Yet, even with hundreds of unique pieces of artwork, it won't feel like you're living through an Infinity War. Delicately executed details, like Manhattan Restaurant's Asgard-inspired chandelier and Spider-Man swinging across the panel screens at Skyline Bar, provide simple city elegance with the lightest touch of Marvel magic.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 17-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    If this hotel reminds you of Walt Disney World's Yacht & Beach Club resorts, you're not mistaken—this 1,098-room Disneyland Paris hotel was inspired by its Florida counterpart. The nautical theming is strong, and it's that seaside charm that keeps parkgoers returning to this waterfront escape. Just a 15-minute walk from the park gates, guests can meet maritime Mickey & Minnie Mouse (who don delightful cruisewear) or indulge in a seafood buffet at the aptly named Cape Cod restaurant. It's modeled after a familiar location back in the States, sure, but after spending the day with princesses, dragons, and superheroes, you may find yourself overjoyed to return to those country club comforts.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 13-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    Craving a bit more theming on your Disneyland Paris trip? Look no further than this national park–inspired escape. It offers lodge-style living perfect for a wintertime trip. Cozy up to the Redwood Bar & Lounge hearth, or in one of the newly renovated rooms with nods to Bambi and Pocahontas, and take in the charms of what Disney does best. Multiple on-site buffets allow you to feast like you've been on the move all day because, well, you likely have.

    Note that this Disney-operated hotel is at the moment undergoing a phased refurbishment. For stays in late 2026 and early 2027, I recommend selecting a refurbished room in The Lodges. Starting in February 2027, construction will move to general hotel spaces, and certain facilities will be temporarily unavailable.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 30-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    Sources indicate that rooms at the boutique Hôtel l’Elysée Val d’Europe are modern and minimal, offering the perfect escape from any theme park chaos. Though it's just a 30-minute walk or a short, free shuttle ride away from the gates, the real perk of being a bit removed is its proximity to the Val d’Europe shopping complex and the designer outlet mall La Vallée Village. With a bounty of discounted prices on luxury brands like Prada, Saint Laurent, and Gucci, you're sure to find a Parisian souvenir that'll rival the array of Mickey Mouse goods sold within the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Nine-minute drive.

    If the City of Lights appeals to you for its style and romance, consider this your ideal hotel. Design-forward rooms with concrete walls, sleek bathrooms, and an open, plant-walled lobby offer reliable value without sacrificing taste, making it a perfect choice for travelers seeking something a little less Disney. While families will benefit from select rooms offering full kitchens and stovetops, the upgraded amenities—which include a heated indoor pool, sauna, and hammam—offer a little something for everyone, just beyond the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 16-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    In a recent development, step right up to this quirky hotel that feels like a Western film set and is jam-packed with Toy Story details. Small touches, like cowprint bedspreads and appearances by Woody and Jessie, make Disney Hotel Cheyenne a hidden gem that's nearly as themed as Disneyland Paris's own Frontierland. Given that it's significantly more affordable than the majority of its Disneyland-owned counterparts yet retains perks like Extra Magic Time, this property offers a best-of-both-worlds approach for those who want to live a full Disney-fied day from first rides to fireworks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute drive.

    Industry observers note that multi-room cabins at this expansive, woodsy resort are the perfect way to experience a taste of the outdoors between trips on Big Thunder Mountain. Sadly, there are no theme park shuttle services, so parks must be reached by car, rideshare, or taxi. But that's not to say it's worth skipping—here, nature abounds in both form and function. There's an on-site aviary, comfort food at the Crockett's Tavern buffet, and plenty of rustic charm, so the comforts of home are never too far away. Consider this Disneyland Paris hotel as close as you can get to camping at Disneyland's theme parks—if camping also included unfettered access to Mickey waffles.

    What area is the best to stay in when visiting Disneyland Paris?

    Any hotel near Disney Village, the entertainment and dining district at the entrance to Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, is going to be the most convenient choice. This not only offers more ease and access, but affords you the option to shop and dine after the parks close each night. Still, booking nearly any Disney-operated hotel will give you benefits like Extra Magic Time and exclusive character encounters, which help get you even more out of your Disneyland Paris vacation.

    Are there any hotels that are walking distance to Disneyland Paris?

    Yes—but you might want to bring your sneakers. Disneyland Hotel is located directly at the entrance to Disneyland Paris, while Disney Hotel New York - The Art of Marvel, Disney Newport Bay Club, and Disney Sequoia Lodge are all a 10- to 15-minute walk through Disney Village to reach both parks. Disney Hotel Cheyenne is a further trek, about 15 to 20 minutes away, but absolutely doable. Shuttle buses are available as well.

    What is the 3-2-1 rule at Disneyland Paris?

    The 3-2-1 rule is essentially shorthand for how to streamline your Disneyland Paris experience. Experts recommend selecting three rides, two entertainment offerings, and one dining option for an easy, straightforward approach to planning a day at any Disney theme park. It works as well at Walt Disney World and Disneyland as it does here at Disneyland Paris, but I recommend you still do a little research before you go. Be sure you don't skip Phantom Manor, which can only be found in Paris, secure your dining reservations early, and don't miss the nighttime highlights offered at both parks—they're among the best in the world.

    It is best to stay within the park at Disneyland Paris, or outside of it?

    Recent findings suggest that it goes without saying that the closer you are to the castle, the “better” your hotel will be, but it shouldn't be a deal-breaker. Convenience is always a factor, but Disney-operated hotels at Disneyland Paris tend to be much pricier than their American counterparts, so staying a bus ride away might be necessary. Still, the perks are plenty across most of Disneyland's own hotels, including extra time in the parks, which is why I recommended so many of them.

    Google Maps: Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres.

    Hyatt is the best in the business at high end resort arrivals. I had given my name at the security gate and by the time I reached the lobby, the door to the vehicle was opened for me, I was greeted by name and a “welcome home”, a constant refrain throughout my stay. It’s a small thing and maybe cliché but it was effective. I was given a Globalist upgrade even though rules at all-inclusives differ from the rest of the chain. As my upgrade was in a Preferred room, I was brought into a private room at the front of the lobby where check-in was done for me.

    The lobby is an open-air room under an arched woven ceiling, with a direct view out to the ocean.

    The resort is spread across 10 buildings with 505 keys. Of those, 221 are Preferred Club keys with an elevated experience. My building (and others like it) had just five rooms on each floor and just five floors which made it feel boutique rather than massive. Every oceanfront room is Preferred Club, and so are the first two buildings on either side.

    In a recent development, the room views follow a simple rule by floor. Every first floor room is a swim-out, floors two through four are tropical view, and the fifth floor is ocean view or ocean front. That makes booking easy to reason through: if you want to step off your patio into the water, go low, and if you want the sea, go high.

    According to recent reports, the walkways give a sense of grandeur and space. All of the flora is local, and in a touch I loved, the service rooms are named after the plants.

    Recent findings suggest that there are four pools, and each one has a unique characteristic. The Jungle pool is drinks only and hidden in the middle of the resort by trees. The Social pool runs activities throughout the day at this adults-only resort for those who want to participate. There is also an infinity pool on the edge of the beach, and then the Preferred Club pool for those staying in that category. These are separate from the first floor swim-outs.

    The spa (hydrotherapy is included for Preferred guests) featured an outdoor circuit that included both hot and cold plunge pools, amongst other therapeutic services.

    The Preferred Club pool was the most frequented, though some images below look more vacant due to rain that rolled through during my opportunity to collect media on my short stay.

    The gym is open to every guest from 6 AM to 8 PM, and it is outfitted with Technogym equipment.

    Recent findings suggest that the spa is open 8 AM to 8 PM with 17 treatment cabins and a beauty salon, and hydrotherapy is included. That last part is the headline. The hydrotherapy space is ridiculous, easily the standout of the entire property for me, and it is the kind of amenity that would make me pick this resort over a competitor down the beach. There are indoor and outdoor showers as well.

    The men’s changing room featured private showers with an option for indoor or outdoor experiences.

    Industry observers note that the theater seats 264 people and hosts cabaret and Mayan shows. There are also pickleball courts, which I am starting to think should be required equipment at any resort that wants a younger crowd as well as padel for the European set (and growing American interest.).

    Industry observers note that secrets is an adults-only brand, and every room here comes with what the tech giant calls Unlimited-Luxury. For a standard guest that means unlimited dining and top-shelf drinks, Wi-Fi, daytime activities and nightly entertainment, with tips and taxes included. Add 24-hour room service, a mini-bar refreshed daily (you can ask for just about anything you want in there), and pool and beach wait service for all guests.

    The Preferred Club is an upgrade, and at this resort it is a substantial one because it owns the oceanfront. Secrets lists personalized check-in and check-out, afternoon hot and cold hors d’oeuvres, desserts and premium liquors, access to the Preferred Club lounge and beach bar, an upgraded mini-bar, upgraded bath amenities, butler service, Bali beds at the pool and beach reserved for club guests, and exclusive dining at the Preferred Club beach restaurant. Preferred also gives club guests exclusive access to an infinity pool and puts an oversized soaking tub on the terrace of the upgraded suites (at least with the oceanfronts).

    According to recent reports, I book a lot of Hyatt’s all-inclusives through Hyatt Privé rates, and this resort is one of 388 in the collection. Privé is Hyatt’s invitation-only program for travel advisors, so you only get the benefits when an approved advisor makes the booking, and the stay still earns World of Hyatt points and elite nights.

    It has been revealed that the all-inclusive version of Privé looks a lot different from a Park Hyatt booking. As I wrote when Hyatt’s all-inclusive resorts joined Privé, there is no room upgrade and no breakfast benefit, since every meal is already included. At this property, Privé guests receive a $100 resort credit per stay, a welcome amenity and letter, hydrotherapy access, and early check-in and late check-out based on availability.

    According to recent reports, elite status matters here more than at most all-inclusives. Under World of Hyatt’s terms, Globalists get the best room available at check-in, including rooms with club access, at the resort’s discretion. Explorists are eligible for upgrades too, but not to standard suites or club rooms. Travelers who have stayed at Secrets resorts as Globalists report being designated Preferred Club guests even when they did not land in a club building, which unlocks the lounge, pool and beach areas. This was my experience on all accounts at the resort. Late checkout is 2 PM for Explorists and 4 PM for Globalists, subject to availability at resorts. It was able to honor my request for a late check-out, I did not arrive early enough to request the early check-in. Hyatt waives resort fees on eligible paid rates (at least for now) and award nights for Globalists, and on award nights only for every other tier, and Globalists also get free parking on free nights though in 2028 Globalists will have to select this as a preference. One catch is that Suite Upgrade Awards cannot be used at Secrets resorts, so you cannot lock in a suite with one here.

    Weddings are significant business here. The courtyard outside the theater is the setting, with the sunset behind it, and the resort hosts lots of them. The resort disclosed its occupancy to me but it wasn’t clear if it was for public consumption. It was shockingly high especially for a Thursday in mid-November. Over the holidays or spring break all the hotels are full but this is a period where I would have expected a lull. Still, despite being extremely full, it never felt crowded.

    For meetings and groups, the convention space measures 9,800 square feet and splits into five sections. The boardroom was occupied at the time so I couldn’t include images of that.

    According to recent reports, restaurants can be booked in advance through the Hyatt Inclusive Collection app, which I wish more all-inclusives offered. Nobody wants to find out at 7 PM that the restaurant they wanted is full and through the app this can be done well in advance of a guest’s arrival. The dress code in the restaurants is resort casual, though the patio does not require slacks and closed toed shoes for men, shorts are acceptable outside.

    According to recent reports, the restaurants include: Portofino (Italian), Bordeaux (French), Himitsu (pan-Asian, with sushi and teppanyaki), Oceana (seafood in an open-air setting), Barefoot Grill (light lunch), Market Café (the international buffet, which I noted on site as the Marketplace), Seaside Grill (a poolside grill), and Coco Café. The bars on that list include Rendezvous in the lobby, Barracuda on the beach, a swim-up bar, a beach bar, and the Preferred Club beach bar and lounge bar. There’s also a Sports Bar and Lounge next to the theater.

    Oceana is the seafood restaurant, set in an open-air dining room with woven pendant lamps, macrame hangings and a pebble mosaic floor. I chose this for my one dinner on property during my brief stay.

    I started with the lamb croquettes, which the menu serves with yogurt and sweet chili sauce, cashews, watercress and a pickled shallot salad, and the Iberian salad with fresh mozzarella, prosciutto, rucula, toasted pistachios, balsamic and roasted peach. A crusty loaf came with the meal.

    For a main I had the coconut shrimp, served with parsley orzo pasta, coconut sauce and parmesan crispy, and finished with the mango cheesecake, which the menu plates with vanilla cream and a mango compote with honey and basil.

    Market Café, the international buffet I noted as the Marketplace, serves breakfast until 11:30 AM. [TO CONFIRM: lunch and dinner service at Market Café].

    Seaside Grill hosts the Preferred Club à la carte breakfast. The official dining page claims breakfast there is served for Preferred Club guests only. I tried a number of dishes for lunch to report to our fine audience.

    Rendezvous sits at the heart of the property with 360-degree access, so you can walk up to it from any direction.

    Preferred Club guests get their own bar at the beach, and the Preferred Club lounge also has an indoor lounge for when the sun gets to be too much.

    My room was a Preferred Oceanfront King, a single open room with a king bed against a macrame headboard wall, rattan pendant lights, a ceiling fan, and a daybed sofa facing a marble bistro table. The balcony with jacuzzi looks straight over the beach. In the bathroom, a freestanding tub sits under a wood-slat ceiling beside a walk-in rain shower with a pebble floor and a bench. The double vanity has vessel sinks, round mirrors and a wave-textured wall, and the shower is stocked with Le Labo Bergamote 22 shampoo, conditioner and shower gel. Le Labo is a confirmed winner for me.

    I also had the chance to tour a master suites, all of which are oceanfront, and they are also available as swim-outs.

    Every first floor room is a swim-out, opening onto the pool.

    According to recent reports, secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres is an incredible resort that somehow felt small when you were in your building but big enough to have everything. For my stay, I used 45,000 points on a no-notice booking to offset a $1,300/night stay. I have seen rates from $560 for off-season which is without question worth it. I loved the property and I look forward to returning with more time and my wife, but the adults-only nature of the property will make it a harder stay for us to achieve.

    Sources indicate that what do you think? Have you stayed at Secrets Playa Blanca Costa Mujeres?

    #122720. Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    Mary Peltola unseats Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov.
    • Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen.
    • In a recent development, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Former Alaska Rep. Mary Peltola speaks during her election night party in Anchorage on Nov. 3. (Charly Triballeau/ AFP via Getty Images).

    Former Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska, giving Senate Democrats their ninth pickup of the midterm elections and bringing their caucus’s total seats in the next Congress to 56.

    In a recent development, the Associated Press called the race for Peltola around 10:19 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday, a full two weeks after Election Day. The latest tranche of ballots counted put the former congresswoman past the 50-percent threshold to win the election outright without Alaska’s ranked choice voting system kicking in.

    With her victory, Peltola, who is Yup’ik, becomes one of the first Native American women elected to the Senate, along with fellow Democrat Peggy Flanagan, who won the open seat in Minnesota this month.

    “As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first.,” Peltola said in a statement after the race was called.

    Recent findings suggest that the Alaska race was the final Senate contest to be called in a midterm election that saw Democrats win commanding majorities in both chambers of Congress. Besides Alaska, Democrats also flipped Senate seats in North Carolina, Maine, Ohio, Texas, Iowa, Kansas, South Carolina and Mississippi.

    In a recent development, peltola, a former state legislator, made history in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to Congress, winning a special election for the state’s at-large district. She comfortably won the general election that fall but was narrowly unseated in 2024 by Republican Nick Begich.

    She entered the Senate contest in January, positioning herself as an independent-minded Democrat and invoking the legacies of two well-liked Alaska Republicans, the late Sen. Ted Stevens and the late Rep. Don Young, whom she succeeded in the House.

    She campaigned on the slogan “fish, family, freedom” and played up her moderate views and deep roots in the state.

    In a recent development, but the race was marked by allegations of political gamesmanship. In addition to the incumbent Sullivan, a retired colonel in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserves, the Senate ballot also included a retired teacher named Dan J. Sullivan. The New York Times reported late last month that operatives aligned with Peltola’s campaign were involved in the effort to recruit the second Dan Sullivan in an attempt to confuse voters.

    Peltola has mentioned she had no connection to the scheme.

    Prior to Election Day, the Trump administration filed a lawsuit seeking to delay certification of the result if Sen. Sullivan were to lose. The lawsuit was tossed earlier this month by a federal judge.

    Sources indicate that trump also suggested that all votes cast for Dan J. Sullivan should be added to the incumbent’s total. “If you add them up, Dan Sullivan wins,” the president told reporters Monday. But as of Tuesday evening when the race was called, Peltola had more votes than both Sullivans combined.

    The Alaska race was initially viewed as a long shot for Democrats. The Last Frontier has elected a Democratic senator just once in the past 50 years – in 2008, when Mark Begich ousted Stevens. Begich, the Democratic uncle of the current Republican congressman, served a single term before he was ousted by Sullivan in 2014.

    But anger in Alaska over the rising cost of food and fuel — already among the highest in the nation — provided Democrats with an opening.

    Industry observers note that "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago," Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer noted in a statement Tuesday night. "But I knew if we concentrated on getting the best candidates, and if we focused like a laser on the costs, corruption, and chaos that Donald Trump has wrought throughout America, we would have shot.".

    In other Alaska races, Democrats flipped the governor’s mansion, with former state Rep. Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins winning an open-seat race to become the first Democrat elected governor of the state since Tony Knowles won a second term in 1998.

    The race for the state’s at-large House district will be decided by ranked choice voting, with tabulations expected to take place Wednesday. Begich, the GOP incumbent, was leading Tuesday with 47.5 percent of the vote and is expected to prevail over independent Bill Hill, who had the backing of national Democrats and trailed with 42 percent. Another Democrat and a Libertarian combined for the remainder of the vote.
